issues.description: Constructor mismatch for class Farm: The problem statement (and the example code in the template Main) require/expect a no-argument constructor (students are instructed to "Initialize the ArrayList in a constructor with no arguments" and the template Main uses new Farm()). The solution repository's Farm class only provides a constructor with a single int parameter (public Farm(int initialCapacity)) and does not provide a no-argument constructor. This prevents code that calls new Farm() (as shown in the template Main and implied by the specification) from compiling against the solution and confuses students about which constructor to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Add a public no-argument constructor to the solution's Farm class that initializes the animals list, e.g. public Farm() { this.animals = new ArrayList<>(); }. You may keep the existing public Farm(int initialCapacity) as an overloaded constructor. Alternatively, make the problem statement and template Main use the existing Farm(int) constructor consistently, but the preferred fix is to provide the no-arg constructor so new Farm() works as specified.

issues.description: Constructor signature mismatch for the Farm class: the exercise text and template expect a no-argument constructor that initializes the internal ArrayList, but the solution only provides a parameterized constructor Farm(int initialCapacity). Specifically: the problem statement (line 108) instructs to “Initialize the ArrayList in a constructor with no arguments”; the template Main.java instantiates the farm with new Farm() (template Main.java, line 14); the template Farm.java contains a TODO and no constructor; the solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java declares only public Farm(int initialCapacity) (lines 11-13). A student following the problem description or using the provided Main would get a compile error because the expected no-arg Farm() constructor is not present in the solution API.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Farm API consistent across artifacts. Preferred fix: add a public no-argument constructor to the solution that initializes the animals list, e.g. public Farm() { this.animals = new ArrayList<>(); } so new Farm() compiles and matches the problem text and template. Alternatively, if an initial-capacity constructor is required pedagogically, update the problem statement and template Main to document and use Farm(int initialCapacity) instead.
